trust_decision.summary: A meter's user-supplied JSONPath must be bound as a ClickHouse query argument, not concatenated into a single-quoted literal; the decision is made in validateJsonPathQuery.toSQL for the v1 create/update routes, and is not made at all in the v3 meter handlers.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'SQL injection through meter creation'; the first thing an engineer reads is the CreateMeter handler, which calls validateJSONPaths before creating the meter.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/v1/meters (CreateMeter) and PUT /api/v1/meters/{meterIdOrSlug} (UpdateMeter), both via streaming.Connector.ValidateJSONPath
fix_sites.module_kind: internal query builder in the ClickHouse streaming connector, reached through the public streaming.Connector interface

O3_reason_to_dismiss: v3 is a separate, newer API surface that delegates straight to the meter service and never called the v1 validator; its stored JSONPath is escaped downstream by escapeJSONPathLiteral, so a solver can argue it was never in the advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The ClickHouse round-trip must keep accepting legitimate JSONPath text (including paths with quotes, brackets and escape characters) and keep returning false only for ClickHouse error code 36; an over-broad fix that strips or rejects quote/backslash characters, or drops the validation call, breaks meter creation for valid paths and stops rejecting invalid ones.

O6_input_shapes: groupBy map[string]string values on create (many JSONPath strings in one request)
JSONPath text containing single quotes, backslashes and double quotes
JSONPath passed as a bound ? argument rather than an embedded literal (the shape introduced by the fix)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/v3/openmeter/meters and PUT /api/v3/openmeter/meters/{meterId} accept value_property/dimensions and store the meter without ever calling streaming.ValidateJSONPath; the stored JSONPath is later interpolated into JSON_VALUE SQL by queryMeter.toSQL.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: v3 is a different API surface whose handlers never used the v1 validator; the stored path is escaped later by escapeJSONPathLiteral, so it can be argued that the advisory's fix never covered this route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate package tree api/v3/handlers/meters, reached through openmeter/meter/service and openmeter/meter/adapter; about 4 files / 3 packages from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A meter JSONPath containing '?' is embedded verbatim in the SQL text, where clickhouse-go treats it as an extra bind placeholder and shifts the argument list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The builder hand-formats JSON_VALUE(...) with fmt.Sprintf for five aggregation branches and does not escape '?'; the same style is repeated at meter_query.go:302.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new aggregation branch or JSONPath consumer that formats JSON_VALUE(...) with fmt.Sprintf and forgets escapeJSONPathLiteral.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: All five existing JSON_VALUE branches are hand-formatted with a manual escaper, so a maintainer adding a branch can copy the format string and omit the escaper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second group-by-values / ad-hoc query written with string interpolation instead of sb.Var.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same package mixes parameter binding here with manual interpolation in meter_query.go, so a new query is likely to copy either style.

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.5 (go.mod:3); standard go build ./... and go test ./...
services: ClickHouse (ValidateJSONPath executes a query; integration tests skip unless TEST_CLICKHOUSE_DSN is set)
PostgreSQL (meter persistence for the full server)
O10_build.project_tests: openmeter/streaming/clickhouse/meter_query_test.go and group_by_values_query_test.go are pure SQL-string unit tests; connector_test.go/suite_test.go are ClickHouse integration tests that skip when TEST_CLICKHOUSE_DSN is unset (suite_test.go:32-35). There is no existing test for ValidateJSONPath; the fix's openmeter/streaming/clickhouse/utils_query_test.go is absent at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep embedding the path in utils_query.go but swap sqlbuilder.Escape for a hand-written quote/backslash escaper (or reuse escapeJSONPathLiteral) instead of binding the value as a ? argument.

out_of_scope_notes: openmeter/streaming/clickhouse/queryhelper.go:30,34,40 interpolate customer IDs/keys and arbitrary (only length-validated) subject keys into a raw WITH map(...) clause using the same sqlbuilder.Escape primitive the fix abandoned; if that primitive is the root cause this is a separate injection surface outside this advisory's JSONPath scope, not pursued.

openmeter/streaming/clickhouse/meter_query.go:353-354 interpolates QuerySettings key/value pairs into a SETTINGS clause; they come from connector config, not user input, so this is outside the advisory's scope.
unverified: The exact defect in github.com/huandu/go-sqlbuilder v1.41.0's Escape (why the old quoted literal was injectable) could not be read: the dependency source is not in the checked-out tree.

Whether escapeJSONPathLiteral (meter_query.go:484-508) fully neutralises ClickHouse string parsing on the O8 v3 route was not verified by executing ClickHouse; if it does, the v3 route is a validation gap rather than a live injection.
Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell access); no tiny_repo/giant_repo judgement was made.
Build and tests were not run (reading only); buildability is inferred from go.mod and the TEST_CLICKHOUSE_DSN skip logic.
